articles.title: Apuestas y pronósticos España vs Croacia
articles.standfirst: 1XBET te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a España y Croacia en el Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán correspondiente a la jornada 2 del Grupo 3 de la Liga A de la Nations League
articles.summary: 1XBET te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a España y Croacia en el Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán correspondiente a la jornada 2 del Grupo 3 de la Liga A de la Nations League
articles.body: España afronta su segundo compromiso de esta Nations League después de protagonizar un estreno de máxima exigencia en Wembley. La selección española consiguió remontar ante Inglaterra para comenzar la competición con una prestigiosa victoria a domicilio, prolongando así la buena dinámica del combinado nacional después de ganar el Mundial. Ahora, buscará mantener ese ritmo ante su afición en un duelo que puede servir para consolidar el liderato del grupo en solitario. Favorito para el partido entre España y Croacia Croacia también llega a esta segunda jornada después de sumar los tres puntos en su estreno. El combinado balcánico derrotó a la República Checa de Santi Denia en un encuentro en el que, además, Luka Modric volvió a dejar su sello en forma de gol. Pese al buen inicio croata, las casas de apuestas conceden un favoritismo muy marcado a España: 1XBET ofrece una cuota de 1.17 por la victoria española, 7.30 por el empate y 15.00 por el triunfo de Croacia. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan presenta una tendencia idéntica en los dos combinados y aparece como una opción a tener en cuenta en las apuestas deportivas. España cumplió este pronóstico en su remontada ante Inglaterra, en un encuentro en el que recibió un gol pero terminó imponiéndose. Croacia también vio marcar a ambos equipos en su victoria frente a la República Checa, por lo que sus respectivos estrenos dejaron un escenario favorable para este mercado. 1XBET ofrece una cuota de 2.14 por el 'sí' y de 1.64 por el 'no'. Número total de goles (Over/Under) La línea de goles también parte de una estadística coincidente entre ambas selecciones. En la victoria de España contra Inglaterra se superaron los 2.5 goles totales, mientras que en el triunfo de Croacia frente a la República Checa también se alcanzó esta barrera. Los dos combinados demostraron capacidad para participar en encuentros con marcadores elevados en su estreno, aunque ahora se medirán en un duelo de mayor exigencia. 1XBET paga a 1.45 que se superen los 2.5 goles y a 2.53 que se registren menos de 2.5 tantos. Goles en ambas mitades El mercado de goles en ambas mitades presenta diferencias entre los dos equipos después de sus respectivos debuts. España cumplió este pronóstico ante Inglaterra, ya que hubo goles tanto antes como después del descanso durante su remontada en Wembley. Croacia, en cambio, no lo hizo frente a la República Checa, puesto que todos los tantos del encuentro llegaron durante la segunda parte. 1XBET ofrece una cuota de 1.44 por que haya gol en ambas mitades y de 2.57 por que no se produzca este escenario.

articles.title: 'Feels like a dream': An Se-young completes badminton's golden sweep with Asian Games triumph over Akane Yamaguchi
articles.summary: An Se-young added another glittering chapter to her extraordinary career on Tuesday, defeating Japan’s three-time world champion Akane Yamaguchi 21-17,
articles.body: An Se-young added another glittering chapter to her extraordinary career on Tuesday, defeating Japan’s three-time world champion Akane Yamaguchi 21-17, 21-9 to win Asian Games gold and underline her status as the world’s No. 1-ranked female badminton player.The South Korean star has now collected virtually every major prize the sport has to offer. Already a Paris Olympic champion and two-time world champion, An has added a second Asian Games gold medal to her collection, further strengthening her extraordinary claim to the top of the women’s game.An dropped to her knees after sealing victory, before arching backwards and looking skyward in an emotional celebration.“It feels like a dream,” An said. “I am so happy and I'm overwhelmed with emotion as I think back to all the hard work I've put in.”Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleAn leaves Yamaguchi chasing shadowsThe final was a demonstration of An’s athleticism, court coverage and relentless pressure. She repeatedly used the full width and depth of the court, forcing Yamaguchi into long, exhausting movements before finding openings to finish points.“I decided to approach the match with the aim of making my opponent feel rushed and forcing her to move around a lot,” An said.Yamaguchi, a three-time world champion, struggled to match An’s pace in the second game as the South Korean surged away to a commanding 21-9 victory.An had earlier defeated China’s Chen Yufei in the semifinals, extending her winning streak against her Chinese rival to five matches.From controversy to another major titleAn’s journey to the top has also included difficult moments. After winning Olympic gold in Paris, she criticised South Korea’s national training system, saying she had been forced to play through a knee injury and questioning some training methods. She later backed away from her threat to pursue an independent path.But on the court, An’s response has been emphatic. articles.title: Vishal TK holds off Thailand as India race to men's 4x400m relay bronze at Asian Games
articles.summary: Indian athletes continued their medal-winning run in track and field at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, with the team of Dharmveer Choudhary, Manu
articles.body: Indian athletes continued their medal-winning run in track and field at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, with the team of Dharmveer Choudhary, Manu T, Jay Kumar and Vishal TK winning bronze in the men's 4x400m relay on Tuesday.The Indian quartet clocked 3:01.61 to finish third in the event. However, the Indian team would be disappointed as they were the defending champions in the event. Nevertheless, it was a commendable performance from the Indian team to finish on the podium.India take bronze with strong runs from Manu T and Vishal TK in 2 and 4; but they could do little to catch up with Japan (gold) and Qatar (silver).Vishal TK kept out Thailand’s Joshua Atkinson in the anchor leg to win bronze.Men's 400m relay - ResultsJapan – 3:00.75Qatar – 3:00.93 (SB)India – 3:01.61Meanwhile, the Indian quartet of Kiran Pahal, Poovamma Machettira, Prachi, and Vithya Ramraj produced an exceptional performance to claim the gold medal on Tuesday in the women's 4x400m relay at the Asian Games.Kiran had a slow start and handed over the baton in third place. Poovamma then made up ground to move India into the lead before Prachi ensured that Vithya received the baton in a similar position.Vithya then produced a strong final leg to hold on to the lead. Bahrain's Salwa Eid Nasser, who received the baton in last place, chased down the runners ahead of her and closed the gap on Vithya, but the Indian held her ground to secure the gold for India. Bahrain and China finished second and third respectively. articles.title: Asian Games 2026 Medal Tally: How two gold medals lifted India back into the top 10
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India’s Asian Games campaign received a significant boost on Tuesday as two gold medals on Day 10 helped the country climb back into the top 10
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s Asian Games campaign received a significant boost on Tuesday as two gold medals on Day 10 helped the country climb back into the top 10 of the medal table. India won eight medals overall, taking its tally to 53 — six gold, 21 silver and 26 bronze — to move into 10th position.The two gold medals came in shooting and athletics, with Neeru Dhanda producing a historic performance in the women’s trap individual event before the Indian women’s 4x400m relay team delivered another top finish.The gold-medal double also ended India’s wait for the top step of the podium after two days without a gold, following the double triumph in kabaddi on September 26.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleNeeru, women’s relay team deliver golden doubleDhanda made history by winning India’s first-ever Asian Games gold in the women’s trap event. Despite incessant rain affecting visibility, she remained composed to finish with 28 hits in the final, setting an Asian Games record. It was also India’s first individual shooting gold of the Games.Athletics then produced another gold as Kiran, Prachi Choudhary, MR Poovamma and Vithya Ramraj won the women’s 4x400m relay in 3:29.69.For Poovamma, the 36-year-old, it was another chapter in her Asian Games career after being part of India’s gold-medal winning relay teams in 2014 and 2018. Vithya added the relay gold to her breakthrough campaign after earlier bettering PT Usha’s more than four-decade-old national record in the 400m hurdles.Eight medals but mixed athletics resultsIndia’s athletics campaign produced a mixed bag, with 19-year-old Pooja Singh winning high jump bronze after clearing 1.84m and Gulveer Singh completing a medal treble with bronze in the 5000m, adding to his silver medals in the 10,000m and 1500m.India also won bronze in the 4x100m mixed relay through Gurindervir Singh, Sneha Sathyanarayana, Animesh Kujur and Harita Bhadra in a season-best 41.06 seconds.The men’s 4x400m relay team of Vishal TK, Dharamveer Choudhary, Jay Kumar and T Manu settled for bronze in 3:01.61, missing out on defending the Hangzhou title.Shooting added another silver in the women’s trap team event, while boxing guaranteed three medals. Narender took bronze after losing his 90+kg semifinal, while Parveen and Ankush Panghal advanced to their respective finals.Two golds lift India back into top 10The twin gold-medal haul proved crucial in the overall standings. India’s 53 medals moved the country back into 10th place, while China continued to dominate with 254 medals.Japan followed with 183 medals, while South Korea and Uzbekistan had 95 and 44 respectively.For India, the biggest takeaway from Day 10 was the return to the top 10, powered by two gold medals that took its overall haul beyond the 50-medal mark.Asian Games Medal Tally after Day 10RankNationGoldSilverBronzeTotal1China14362492542Japan4571671833South Korea242744954Uzbekistan141713445Thailand12912336Bahrain1154207Iran101611378Kazakhstan91425489North Korea7561810INDIA6212653Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
